title: Bernadette in the convent
hookLine: asked about Lourdes, she says she was used like a broom and put back

cards: A visitor at a convent door in Nevers, in the middle of France, hopes for a glimpse of the well-known one.
Back in Lourdes, the grotto where she knelt is drawing crowds, a church is rising above it, and the sick are coming to the spring.
Here, far to the north, the girl at the center of it all is sweeping, folding linen, helping in the infirmary, and often sick in bed herself.
When people press her about what she saw, she gives an answer that sounds almost like a joke. It is about a broom.

teach.b: Bernadette Soubirous, the girl who said a lady appeared to her at the grotto of Lourdes, did not stay in Lourdes. She joined the Sisters of Charity of Nevers and left her home town for their mother house. First, leaving.
At Lourdes she could not walk down a street without being stared at, questioned, asked to touch rosaries. In the convent she asked to be one sister among many. Second, the broom.

teach.h: A BROOM, PUT BACK IN ITS PLACE.
teach.b: Her fellow sisters remembered her saying something like this: the Virgin used me like a broom; when you've finished sweeping, you put the broom back in its place, in the corner, behind the door. That's where I am now.
She did not see herself as the point of the story. The lady was, and the message. She was the tool, and the tool had been put away.
She was often ill, for long stretches, and tradition remembers her calling illness her work. She helped as a nurse's aide and in the sacristy when she was able.
Some of the sisters in charge were hard on her, and she bore it quietly.

teach.h: A SAINT FOR HOW SHE LIVED.
teach.b: Fourth, why she is a saint. The Church canonized her for how she lived, not simply for what she reported seeing.
Mary's own song in Luke's Gospel says it in the Douay-Rheims: "Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid." Regarded. Seen.
Bernadette's holiness, in the Church's eyes, was mostly hidden, in a convent, in a sickbed, like a broom behind the door.

how: Catholics keep Saint Bernadette's feast in April, and pilgrims to Lourdes often also visit the convent chapel at Nevers, where her body lies in a glass reliquary.

games.q: you are the girl from Lourdes. people everywhere want to see you, hear the story, touch your rosary. what do you do?
o: travel and tell the story to crowds.
join a convent far away and live as one sister among many.
stay at the grotto and greet the pilgrims.

practice: Think of a time you did something that mattered and nobody noticed, or wanted credit and didn't get it. Picture a broom leaning in a corner behind a door after the floor is swept: useful, then put back.
If you pray, offer that unseen thing to God; if you don't, let it be enough that it was done.

wordCard.voice: Bernadette Soubirous. The visionary of Lourdes, who became an ordinary sister in Nevers and said she had been used like a broom and put back in the corner.

carryVoice: Your line: put back in the corner. The lady was the point, never the broom. See you tomorrow.
